#1741. Boston was a lovely holiday romance, but let's leave it there. Talk of taking Tartan Army back there every two years is just cringeworthy

Published: 11:18 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 13:03 EST, 13 November 2026

Boston was the loveliest little holiday romance. An unforgettable moment in time. But let’s just leave it at that, shall we?

Can’t we just allow those involved in the shenanigans around the World Cup last summer to reflect misty-eyed on doorways to Xanadu being opened by the tilt of the kilt and maybe even the heady nights they can’t remember much about at all?

Or does everything have to be milked to the max these days? Flogged like a dead horse to benefit someone or other. Ruined, really. Played out until every scintilla of fun has been drained out of it.

A bit like Yes, Sir, I Can Boogie. That started out as a bona-fide hoot. A half-cut Andy Considine dressing up in drag with his friends and family during his stag do in London in 2015 and making a music video around Baccara’s 1977 hit. It went viral. Obviously. It was – and is – hilarious.

When Scotland’s players resurrected it in the dressing room in Serbia five years later – with Considine as part of the squad – after the national team had ended a 23-year wait to make it to a major competition, it was simply inspired.

Every second of those infectious scenes exuded elation, joy, togetherness and pin-sharp humour, a killer recipe for the interludes that make life and living so great.

Now? Even the opening bars of the song bring on a sense of dread. It was splattered over T-shirts, played everywhere on repeat and still gets aired at every Scotland home game.

The Tartan Army march to Boston's Fenway Park baseball stadium

It’s boring. It’s been done to death and now lives firmly in that grim, stagnant swamp known as Scottish mainstream culture along with munchy boxes, Bitz N Pieces, theatre shows about the Old Firm and ex-footballers suddenly developing a personality and getting involved in stage shows to tell the world how Wee Dazza once did Big Jazza a beauty in the dressing-room by leaving a squelchy banana in his shoe. The banter anawrat.

Everything ends up spoiled here and it looks like we’re already well down that road with the Tartan Army thanks to the news breaking that the Scottish FA are in talks with the State of Massachusetts over a biennial friendly match at the Gillette Stadium, the black hole amid the festivity at the finals thanks to struggling past Haiti and embarrassing ourselves against Morocco.

State senator Paul Feeney has been across the pond to press the flesh. Massachusetts senate president Karen Spilka is already talking about staging Tartan Day – presumably some rip-off of that twee, shortbread-tin abomination in New York – and ‘other events’.

The heart sinks. Listen, the minute politicians get involved in any kind of ‘happening’, the best thing to do is give it a wide berth.

Mind you, before the Big Swerve, it might be worthwhile having someone remind these characters from The Bay State that Massachusetts’ first contribution to Scotland supporters hitting town in summer involved hiking the cost of the 25-mile train ride from Boston to the ground from $20 to a ludicrous $80.

What unfolded there in mid-June was nothing to do with them. It was everything to do with spontaneity. As it ought to be. A glorious coming-together of all sorts of folk up for a right, royal carry-on.

There were so many glorious vignettes. Scotland punters taking over Red Sox games. Bars running out of beer. Mass marches. Local women, doped-up on Outlander, telling TikTok how a bunch of jakeys intent on drinking anything within arm’s reach – except Bud Light, of course – were making them feel ‘seen’.

The Tartan Army make their presence known in Boston during the summer's World Cup

It was brilliant. A short spell in which stars aligned and magic happened. Boston had everything the Tartan Army required. And going by the testimony of Bostonians, the Tartan Army brought badly needed vitality back to the streets of a city quietened by Covid and other factors.

Everybody won. Everyone there still dines out on the memory. But that’s where it should stay. In the memory. These conversations about trying to recapture that spirit, recreate it every two years around some meaningless friendly against opposition unconfirmed and possible business meetings on the periphery, feel quite sad. How can it have any legs long-term?

Joe and Josephine Punter have moved on. They’re on the batter in other places now. Next week, it’s Switzerland for a Nations League game. After that, it’s wherever the draw for the Euro qualifiers throws them. New cities. New adventures. As football away days ought to be. In, out, shake it all about.

Away days are not about teaming up with suit-wearing dignitaries to be paraded at the town hall, like performing seals in plaid – even though there does appear to be an element of the Scotland support that enjoys that kind of thing.

Away days are not about being used as political capital or forming part of some constructed ‘festival’.

Look, in most aspects of life, it’s generally best not to go back. Sticking traffic cones on top of statues all over town won’t be as funny next time. There won’t be a 20,000-strong travelling support spending their life savings on games an entire generation had been waiting for. There won’t be anything like the same buzz, if any.

Some folk might fancy returning once, just to see if it feels the same. The idea that this is going to be a big deal every two years, though, feels deeply misguided.

Boston’s Irish. Not Scottish. That Tartan Week nonsense in New York is a toe-curlingly awful melange of kilts, Scottie dogs and actors living in America telling everyone back home how to vote.

No self-respecting Scot should give it house room. If there is a plan for the same thing in Boston, the same rules apply.

Like NYC, it’ll suit those from the political class in the mood for a junket, of course. John Swinney will already be counting the air miles if there’s another game in Massachusetts to go to.

The public, of course, is still counting the cost of the First Minister’s last trip there for the World Cup. The bill came in at £45,000 for him and two senior aides to fly business class. The entire trip for government staff came to more than £98,000.

Swinney plays the role with aplomb at these affairs, supping a pint in his Scotland top. The Scottish Football Association need to ask themselves this, though: why should they put themselves at the heart of some kind of cock-eyed project to build bridges politically?

The Tartan Army leave their signature traffic cone in a park in Boston

First up, the players are hardly likely to welcome a pointless week in America being added to a jam-packed schedule. More importantly, though, what exactly has this SNP-led administration, outwith giving a few bob to grassroots, done for Scottish football down the years?

From this vantage point, they’ve been no friend to the national game or its followers. The Offensive Behaviour at Football Act, repealed in 2018, was a scandalous piece of legislation that criminalised fans and made going to football unpleasant.

Clubs have had to fight tooth and nail to secure trials to sell pints inside stadiums when other sports are allowed to do what they like. After trouble in Glasgow city centre ahead of the Old Firm League Cup final two years ago, Swinney stated that ‘the clubs have got a responsibility to make sure their fans behave properly’.

Inside their grounds, yes. What are they meant to do, though, about teenagers running amok on Argyle Street?

Looking after that is the job of the police. Of course, anyone reading 1919 magazine, funded by the Scottish Police Federation, earlier this year will have noted an article about policing around football being ‘chaotic’ and understaffed because of SNP Government budget cuts.

Just like everything else in this sorry little nation built on buying votes for ‘free stuff’, Police Scotland is creaking at the seams. Why would anyone want to get involved in another transatlantic piece of theatre selling some false, outdated, vaguely comical vision of it to foreigners?

A pointless Scotland friendly – served up as part of some forced, hackneyed ‘cultural exchange’ or not – is hardly an idea to be getting on board with.

Pure dead brilliant, it won’t be. More like pure cringe.

#1740. Arsenal, Liverpool, Chelsea Chase £100m England Midfielder

Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea have all contacted Bournemouth about England midfielder Alex Scott, according to CaughtOffside, which cites The i Paper. Liverpool and Chelsea want to move in January, while Arsenal would rather wait until next summer. Bournemouth’s stance on selling the 23-year-old has softened, but the reported asking price is above £100m, and Scott turned down two contract offers over the summer.

The interest has clear reasons behind it. Andoni Iraola coached Scott at Bournemouth before taking over at Anfield in June, and Liverpool want to reunite them. Chelsea lost Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City in a £125m deadline-day deal and had a reported £64m bid for Scott rejected earlier in the summer. Arsenal already have Declan Rice, Bruno Guimaraes, Martin Zubimendi and Myles Lewis-Skelly, so CaughtOffside sees Chelsea or Liverpool as the more logical destinations for his playing time.

Scott wins the ball, presses and carries it through midfield, and he started Bournemouth’s first five league games this season before a quadriceps injury on England duty in October kept him out for weeks. Fitness is the first concern, because knee problems have interrupted much of his time on the south coast. End product is the second. He has scored five league goals in 85 appearances since joining in 2023, so he will not solve a shortage of chances alone.

Not at £100m, and not as a January priority. Liverpool rank 18th for big chances after ten league games, according to This Is Anfield, and Scott offers energy rather than creativity. The real gap sits beside Ryan Gravenberch, where Curtis Jones left in the summer, and nobody arrived to share the defensive work.

Scott could be the aggressive partner in Iraola’s double pivot, freeing Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz to play higher, yet that is a heavy fee for a player only just rebuilding match fitness, with Liverpool fourth and nine points behind Arsenal.

Chelsea’s case is simpler. The division’s biggest summer spenders lost their midfield engine and can justify the price more easily. Arsenal’s patience makes sense, since Rice, Guimaraes and Zubimendi leave no room for a £100m squad player. A Liverpool bid would only inflate the market Chelsea are already shaping. If Iraola wants a January signing, a specialist holding midfielder for far less money does more for the top-four push.

#1739. Liverpool Transfer News: Dutch Star’s Agent Tests Market

Liverpool transfer news: Ryan Gravenberch’s agent, José Fortes Rodriguez, is exploring ways to take his client out of Anfield, according to CaughtOffside. The site relays a claim from the X account @ITKSpace that Fortes has held “loose but direct contact” with several European clubs, none of them named. No formal exit request has been lodged, and the 24-year-old could still stay, so this reads like a camp checking the market rather than a player pushing to leave.

Liverpool hold the stronger hand. His six-year extension, signed in March, runs to 2032, so any buyer would face a substantial asking price. Real Madrid have been linked before, though nothing here says they are interested now.

Iraola’s 4-2-3-1 relies on two central midfielders, and Gravenberch, so commanding at the base of Arne Slot’s title-winning side, has struggled to settle. Iraola benched him for three straight games at one stage, he collected a second yellow card in the 3-0 home defeat by Manchester City on 11 October, and a heel problem has since kept him out of the Arsenal and Fenerbahçe games. He has no goals and one assist in the league this term.

His strengths are clear. At 6ft 3in he carries the ball through pressure and starts attacks from deep. Defending space and tracking runners is the weakness, and it shows when his partner also surges forward.

No, not this winter and not at a price set by his worst few weeks. Gravenberch is 24, tied down until 2032, and his market value has slipped sharply since last December, so selling now would hand a buyer the bargain that March contract was meant to rule out.

The real problem sits elsewhere. Iraola received no new midfielder in the summer, and his double pivot has no natural holding player. Gravenberch has admitted he prefers the number eight role, yet Mac Allister and Szoboszlai, who started the 3-1 win at Crystal Palace that lifted Liverpool to fourth, already occupy those spots. Nineteen-year-old Trey Nyoni has mostly played the deeper role this season.

Keep him through January, get him fit, and judge him again in a settled pairing. If Liverpool then sign a proper holding midfielder next summer, Gravenberch becomes a surplus eight, and a big-club bid at the right figure would deserve a hearing. Selling before that signing arrives just removes the one midfielder who can still carry the ball out of pressure.

#1738. Villa Midfielder Has £80m Price Tag For Arsenal: Is He Worth It?

Arsenal transfer news: Aston Villa do not regard Boubacar Kamara as available, even with Arsenal interested, according to CaughtOffside. The report says an offer of around £80m could change that stance, although Villa negotiate from strength because the 26-year-old’s contract runs until 2030.

January looks highly unlikely. Villa have already lost Amadou Onana to a torn ACL suffered at the World Cup, and the Belgian is not expected back until around April. Unai Emery cannot lose a second holding midfielder in the middle of a season. The summer is different. CaughtOffside says Villa could entertain a significant bid then, provided they can reinvest the money in a proper replacement and strengthen the squad around him.

TBR Football reported in July 2025 that he sat on Arsenal’s long list of midfield targets, and his numbers explain why. Kamara has started all 10 of his Premier League games this season, completing 86.3% of his passes, including 83 line-breaking balls, while making 28 tackles and 40 recoveries. He wins 56% of his duels and can play at centre-back, which would give Mikel Arteta cover in two positions.

The weaknesses are just as clear. He has no goals this season, only three shots and an xG of 0.14, and he has committed 20 fouls and conceded a penalty. He also missed the closing weeks of 2024/25 through injury.

The role he would play is obvious: a ball-playing six next to Declan Rice. Martín Zubimendi occupies it now, and Arsenal lead the league with 27 points from 10 games, six clear of Manchester City, with seven clean sheets.

No, not at that price. Arsenal spent £75m on Bruno Guimarães in August, and Arteta still has Rice, Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Martin Ødegaard and Myles Lewis-Skelly competing for the same central spaces.

FotMob values him at €49m, roughly £43m, so Villa would be asking close to double his market value for a player who turns 27 this month and offers little in the final third. Villa’s insistence on reinvesting the fee also hands them the leverage, which means Arsenal would pay a premium on a seller’s timetable.

The only sensible trigger is a departure, perhaps Zubimendi or the 30-year-old Merino, leaving Arsenal short of a proven Premier League six. Kamara is a better holding midfielder than most of the market, but a title-leading side already has that job covered, and £80m would buy cover rather than improvement.

#1737. Chelsea’s £43m Winger Gamble Is Stalling: Should They Accept A Discount?

Chelsea transfer news: Birmingham Live reports that Alejandro Garnacho’s future needs resolving, because the winger has not started a match for Aston Villa and a permanent move depends on certain conditions being met. Chelsea sent the 22-year-old to Villa Park on a season-long loan in July, with a reported £43m obligation to buy next summer. Neither club has revealed the trigger, and reports link it to appearances.

The numbers explain the concern. FotMob lists four Premier League outings, all from the bench, without a goal or assist, while Football365 counts only 95 minutes across seven substitute appearances. Football Insider claims Villa are prepared to back out of the deal if his form doesn’t improve.

Garnacho’s strengths haven’t changed. His pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders earned a £40m move from Manchester United in 2025. The weakness is end product, and it followed him to London with eight goals in 43 games for Chelsea, only one of them in 24 Premier League appearances. Unai Emery left him out of the squad for the Manchester United game.

Chelsea have no obvious use for him either. Xabi Alonso told him in July that regular football wasn’t guaranteed, and the 3-4-2-1 Alonso favours uses Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer behind João Pedro, with Pedro Neto and Estêvão competing for the wide roles.

FotMob values him at about €29m (roughly £25m), far below the €71m peak recorded in August 2024, and Manchester United are reportedly entitled to 10 per cent of any future fee. If the clause isn’t triggered, he returns in July 2027 on a contract running to 2032.

Yes, and soon. Chelsea built the deal to protect £43m, but the clause relies on appearances from a manager who isn’t picking him, so the price drops with every unused substitution. The sporting case for a return is thin. Alonso’s system asks wide players to defend as wing-backs, while Garnacho’s value lies in isolating a full-back, and the £117m Rogers signing already covers the left-sided attacking role.

A mid-£20m sale, even after United’s cut, would still return more than half of the £40m Chelsea paid and clear a contract running to 2032. Chelsea should open talks with Villa in January about a lower fixed fee, or line up other buyers for the summer. A clause that depends on a manager picking a player he has benched was never a safe way to protect £43m.

#1736. Rayan to Liverpool or Manchester United? How the Brazilian’s style suits both clubs

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 18:16

Rayan is living a fast-moving career in European football. Signed by Bournemouth in January 2026 after standing out at Vasco da Gama, the Brazilian forward quickly won a place in the Premier League and began attracting the attention of bigger clubs. Liverpool are already monitoring his progress, while a statement has put Manchester United in the conversation: the player revealed that he has always supported the Red Devils because of Cristiano Ronaldo.

Andoni Iraola, who worked with Rayan at Bournemouth, took charge of Liverpool at the start of 2026-27. Manchester United have just appointed Mauricio Pochettino, a manager known for developing young attackers and for implementing a high-intensity style. But which of the two clubs would be the better destination for the Brazilian? The answer depends less on Rayan’s personal preference and more on the characteristics that have made him one of the most interesting prospects in Brazilian football.

Bournemouth paid Vasco €35m (about £30m) in January 2026, betting on a 19-year-old forward. Adaptation was quick: Rayan scored five goals and provided two assists in 15 games in the second half of last season.

His profile is different from a traditional winger who relies on short dribbles and quick changes of direction to beat a marker. Rayan is a player of strength and acceleration. When he receives with space, he can carry the ball at speed, protect possession with his body and attack the box with few touches.

In the 2025 Brazilian Serie A, Rayan was the player who finished the most carries with a shot, with 33 occasions. He also scored 14 goals in the league, a number that placed him among the competition’s top scorers. The forward is not just a winger who cuts inside, however. Under Fernando Diniz at Vasco, he was also used centrally, as a centre-forward, and showed an ability to win aerial balls and shield possession with his back to goal. His height and physical strength make it possible to imagine growth in that role, although he still has to improve his control and combination play under pressure.

It is also important to consider what is left to develop. Rayan can still improve the quality of his final pass, his choice of moments to shoot and his involvement in building play. Despite the volume of carries that ended in shots, his creative output was more limited. That helps explain why he still needs an environment that gives him freedom to attack without requiring him to be the main organiser of the attack.

This season, the Brazilian has played ten Premier League games, with one goal and no assists. The output does not match his arrival in England, but Rayan remains a frequent starter and is still adapting to a new manager and a model different from Iraola’s.

Liverpool’s interest strengthened after Iraola’s arrival. The Reds followed the Brazilian closely early in the season and could consider a move in 2027. Iraola knows Rayan’s virtues and limitations. It was under his management that the Brazilian began adapting to the intensity of the Premier League, playing mainly on the right and being given freedom to attack space.

The manager also played a part in the step up of other Bournemouth players, such as Antoine Semenyo, who stood out before moving to Manchester City. Tactically, the combination makes sense. Iraola’s teams usually press high, try to win the ball back in advanced areas and accelerate as soon as they find space. He does not demand that his wingers stay tied to the touchline: they can attack inside, combine with the full-backs and appear in different channels. Rayan could play on the right, cutting inside onto his left foot, but also attack depth and offer a physical threat in transitions.

At Liverpool, that characteristic could be useful. The team has changed in attack: Bradley Barcola, Cody Gakpo, Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha offer alternatives, but Rayan would add a different profile, a more powerful forward able to carry the ball at speed and attack the box.

There is one caveat. Liverpool already have quality attacking options. The manager also has to manage a more demanding calendar and a team with title ambitions. Rayan could find a way to play, but would hardly have the same freedom as a young player developing at Bournemouth.

Rayan’s link with Manchester United came to light in an interview with ESPN. The forward said he has always supported the club in England because of Cristiano Ronaldo, his great idol. He also recalled the emotion of playing at Old Trafford and beating the Red Devils 3-0 with Bournemouth in October.

The statement became relevant when United hired Pochettino to try to reorganise a team going through a difficult season. The Argentinian has a track record of developing young players and built his best work in England with intense teams, aggressive in the press and quick in transitions. His most usual model starts from a 4-2-3-1, with wingers who often attack inside spaces and full-backs who push on to give width.

That structure could favour Rayan. Starting from the right, the Brazilian would have freedom to carry towards the box, finish with his left foot and attack the spaces created by team-mates’ movement. High pressing also suits his physical ability, although defensive involvement is still an area he needs to improve.

The problem is competition. United already have Bryan Mbeumo, Amad Diallo and Matheus Cunha among their attacking options, plus Benjamin Sesko as a central reference. There is also a developmental question. Pochettino usually demands a lot from his players without the ball and works with coordinated attacking movements. For a forward who still needs to improve decision-making and creation, the environment can be positive but also brings high demands. The Brazilian would need to learn to alternate individual carrying with quick combination play and movement without the ball.

United, on the other hand, could offer room to grow if Pochettino sees Rayan as a medium-term project and not an immediate solution to attacking problems. The Argentinian’s ability to develop young forwards is a point in favour, but the squad already has players in similar roles.

Between the two scenarios, Liverpool appear to offer the clearer fit. Iraola already knows the Brazilian, knows how to use his strength in transitions and has a model that favours attackers able to carry the ball at speed. The departure of Mohamed Salah has also opened space for a reorganisation of the right side, making the position a concrete possibility for Rayan.

Manchester United have the emotional appeal and a manager whose philosophy could match the Brazilian’s characteristics. But the presence of Mbeumo, Amad and Cunha makes the battle for space more complex. To turn admiration for the club into a transfer, Rayan would need to see a clear sporting plan.

At any rate, the moment is still one of development. At 20, the forward does not need to choose immediately between two giants, especially as he has a contract with Bournemouth until 2031 and is still gaining experience in a demanding league. Rayan has the attributes to reach a top-level club, but his next step needs to be defined by the project that best uses his potential. Between his familiarity with Iraola and his identification with United, Liverpool appear to have a tactical advantage.

#1735. Mirabelli reminisces on Calhanoglu signing and Milan disappointment: “A bitter taste”

Today, Massimiliano Mirabelli has looked back on his time at AC Milan and his favourite signing from his short time with the club.

After arriving before the 2017 summer transfer window, there was hope that Mirabelli would oversee a new era with Milan. However, he never got given the extended period to oversee that change that he’d hoped for.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Indeed, just a year later, the Elliott fund arrived and he was removed from his role as the Rossoneri truly entered a new era.

Responsible for the signings of Andre Silva, Andrea Conti and most notably Leonardo Bonucci, you wonder what would’ve happened if he’d stayed with the Rossoneri for longer. Nevertheless, with what and who eventually arrived, there’s no point considering the alternative, especially given he took a four-year break after his time with the club.

Speaking to Tuttosport, via MilanNews, Mirabelli spoke about the disappointment of his time with the Rossoneri and his pride in bringing Hakan Calhanoglu to Italy.

“Unfortunately, the experience in Milan was short-lived due to the change of ownership. It left a bitter taste in our mouths because we weren’t given the opportunity to complete a long-term project.

“Roma wasn’t built in a day… The deal that still makes me proud today? The Calhanoglu deal . Without a doubt, the best and most successful gamble of my career. We’re talking about the man who, for me, remains the most complete midfielder in Europe to this day. He has incredible, uncommon qualities.

“I started following him when I worked at Inter. We couldn’t sign him from Leverkusen due to an ongoing lawsuit over his double registration as a minor, which resulted in his suspension.

“That’s why I call it a “gamble”: I wanted him at Milan at all costs, even though he hadn’t played for a year and had essentially disappeared from the radar. I was heavily criticized. But, I repeat, I was convinced I had a boy with enormous potential on my hands.

“The biggest discussion, then, was about his position. We spent hours with Montella and—later—with Gattuso to understand where he could best express himself. At Leverkusen, he’d played everywhere: as a midfielder, as an attacking midfielder, and even as a winger.

“Initially, we played him on the left flank, with an inverted foot, to allow him to cut inside and shoot. But it was clear to me that he had all the makings of a great playmaker. When I suggested it to the right people, they called me crazy…

“Leaving for zero? Don’t make me think about it… It’s unspeakable, unbelievable.”

#1734. Liverpool Open Talks With Argentine Midfielder: Is He Worth A New Deal?

Liverpool transfer news: Liverpool have opened contract talks with Alexis Mac Allister, according to @tribuna_ftbl, with his current deal running until June 2028. The report arrives days after his father, Carlos, told ESPN that no discussions had started, although he hinted at news before the end of the year.

It also reverses the summer, when the club extended Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai but made no offer to the 27-year-old, something Mac Allister revealed in September while admitting he had stayed despite chances to leave.

His form explains the change. After a poor 2025/26 under Arne Slot, he has become Andoni Iraola’s first-choice midfielder alongside Szoboszlai, pushing Gravenberch to the bench. He has scored once in the Premier League and three times in the Champions League, including the winner against Atlético Madrid, and holds a 7.29 FotMob average rating across 758 league minutes. Liverpool sit fourth.

FotMob places him in the 88th percentile among midfielders for shot attempts, and he has said the man-to-man system suits him because it demands less communication than Slot’s approach. His weaknesses are just as clear.

His defensive contributions (45th percentile) and aerial duels (46th) sit below the midfield average, and pundit David Lynch has questioned whether his legs have gone in Iraola’s 4-4-2, where two central midfielders cover huge areas. He has also collected four league yellow cards already.

Yes, but not on the terms his summer rebound might demand. Ten league games of good form do not cancel a season in which he looked off the pace, so Liverpool should offer around three years, with wages pitched below the bumper deals Gravenberch and Szoboszlai signed.

The timing still makes sense. With 18 months left, he enters the final year next summer, when Liverpool would face either a discounted sale or a free departure. His FotMob valuation of €66m has almost halved from the €130m peak of September 2025, so selling now would lock in the lowest price.

Iraola also needs a controller to sit beside Szoboszlai’s runs, and no one in the squad does that better. The caveat is that Mac Allister turns 28 next month, so Liverpool must pair him with a quicker partner next summer rather than treat his renewal as the end of the midfield rebuild.

#1731. Declan Rice’s new five-year deal to 2031 marks his rise from £105m signing to Arsenal leader

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 18:28

Declan Rice’s new contract with Arsenal recognises a transformation built over three seasons. When he arrived at the Emirates Stadium in July 2023, the midfielder was a high-impact signing: he cost £105m, a record for a British player at the time, and carried the expectation of lifting a team that had just lost the Premier League title to Manchester City.

Today, at 27, Rice is an English champion, one of the leaders of the dressing room and one of the team’s technical reference points. The new five-year deal shows Arsenal’s intention to keep him at the centre of the project through his physical and technical peak. It also reflects his changing status within the club, as Rice is expected to earn a salary close to that of Bukayo Saka, until now the squad’s top earner.

Rice was not just an expensive signing who lived up to expectations. He became a more complete player, widened his influence across different phases of play and took on responsibilities beyond his role in midfield. The promise of 2023 has become one of the faces of a championship team and a leader for the cycle that starts now.

Rice’s arrival came at a decisive moment for Mikel Arteta’s project. In 2022-23, Arsenal spent much of the season at the top but lost steam in the closing stretch and finished five points behind Manchester City. The team had shown that they could compete for the title, but they needed more quality, depth and experience to sustain a challenge to the end.

Rice had characteristics that answered several of those needs. At 24, he was already West Ham United’s captain, had experience with England and had just won the Conference League. Arsenal beat the competition and completed the signing for £100m fixed plus £5m in bonuses.

The fee raised expectations. It was not enough for Rice to be a good holding midfielder: he had to justify a historic investment and help Arsenal take the step needed to compete with City. His first season showed the scale of the signing quickly.

Rice played 38 Premier League games, scoring seven goals and providing eight assists. The number of goal contributions was a considerable improvement on his West Ham record, but his impact was not limited to attacking output. Arsenal again finished as runners-up, but Rice had already become one of the team’s most important players. The signing did not deliver an immediate title, but it helped turn expectation into a conviction that the club had found a midfielder able to carry their project for many years.

Rice’s development also reflects the way Arteta changed his use. Early in his time at Arsenal, the Englishman often played as the deepest midfielder, responsible for protecting the defence and offering a reference point for build-up. It was a familiar role, close to the one he had at West Ham, but it did not use his full repertoire.

After an adaptation period, especially from the start of 2024, Arteta began using him more often as a box-to-box midfielder on the left. The change let Rice use one of his main qualities: carrying the ball at speed, breaking lines and arriving in the opposition area while still contributing to defensive recovery.

The Englishman gained more freedom to attack space, appear at the edge of the box and join attacking combinations. His physical power became a weapon for taking Arsenal into the opposition half, while his ability to get back helped keep balance when the team lost the ball. Instead of just protecting team-mates, Rice also began to drive the team.

Set pieces were another important tool. Rice began taking corners and free-kicks, using the accuracy of his delivery and his ability to put the ball in dangerous areas. Since his arrival, he has provided ten assists from set pieces in the Premier League. His two free-kick goals against Real Madrid in the 2024-25 Champions League quarter-finals were the most emblematic moment of that evolution.

Versatility does not mean Rice has no fixed position or needs to take part in every attacking action. The most recent development lies in choosing moments. With Martin Zubimendi, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Martin Odegaard offering different partnership options, Arteta has alternated the height at which the Englishman receives the ball and the freedom he has to advance.

The ability to perform different roles is one of the reasons Rice has become so important to Arteta. In the title-winning season, he was used both as the most advanced midfielder and in a midfield pair alongside Zubimendi. He is not just a player who adapts to different positions: he lets the manager change the structure of the team without necessarily changing personnel.

Rice’s growth was not only tactical. Over the seasons, he also became one of the squad’s main voices. His direct personality, willingness to demand more from team-mates and ability to take responsibility in difficult moments made him a reference point for the group.

One example came in April, when Odegaard was out injured and Rice was given the captain’s armband. He had worn it on other occasions, but the choice reinforced a perception that had been building: his influence does not depend on being the official captain.

In Arsenal’s 2025-26 Premier League title, which ended a 22-year wait for the competition, Rice was one of the protagonists of the campaign, with 36 appearances, four goals and five assists in the league. More than his statistical contribution, his ability to maintain intensity in different roles was fundamental.

Declan Rice at Arsenal - all competitions since joining in July 2023 2023-24: 51 games, 48 starts, 33 wins, 8 draws, 10 defeats, 7 goals, 9 assists (64.7% wins) 2024-25: 52 games, 48 starts, 28 wins, 16 draws, 8 defeats, 9 goals, 10 assists (53.8% wins) 2025-26: 55 games, 49 starts, 37 wins, 12 draws, 6 defeats, 5 goals, 9 assists (67.3% wins) 2026-27 (in progress): 15 games, 14 starts, 13 wins, 1 draw, 1 defeat, 1 goal, 5 assists (86.7% wins) Total: 173 games, 159 starts, 111 wins, 37 draws, 25 defeats, 22 goals, 33 assists (64.2% wins)

Trophies for Arsenal (3): Premier League 2025-26, Community Shield 2023, Community Shield 2026

Official matches only (Premier League, Champions League, FA Cup, EFL Cup and Community Shield). Matches decided on penalties count as draws. Data up to 16 November 2026. Sources: FBref (Opta data), BeSoccer and Opta Analyst.

The challenge now is to sustain this level without ignoring fatigue. Rice has come from seasons with a high volume of games, often exceeding 50 matches for club and country. Last season, he played 54 games for Arsenal in all competitions, in addition to England commitments. Managing his workload will be important for him to keep his influence over a demanding calendar.

By extending his contract to 2031, Arsenal secure a player who still has years at his peak ahead and who already knows Arteta’s demands in depth. The club no longer need to wait for Rice to become a leader: that stage has already happened. Now the expectation is that he helps lead the next chapters of a project that intends to keep competing for the main trophies.

#1730. This AI ‘mechanic’ can peer inside the black box of other neural networks

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Some AI models behave like mechanics — fixing issues in other models that they neither designed nor fully understand. Credit: Mint Images/Getty

Researchers have used an artificial-intelligence model to read and tinker with the internal workings of another AI network — offering a new way to peek into the ‘black box’ of AI.

Computer scientists usually improve models by training them in tiny increments or by building them from scratch. A team at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in Cambridge has demonstrated how an AI model called GPT-6 Astra can interpret the raw internal values of some other models well enough to predict what different parts of the systems do. It can then edit the models to make improvements — including boosting their mathematical abilities. The authors reported their findings in a preprint1 on 2 November.

ChatGPT is a black box: how AI research can break it open

ChatGPT is a black box: how AI research can break it open

Frontier AI models are “showing early sparks” of an ability to treat neural networks like files that they can read, reason about and change, says co-author Rikiya Takehi, a machine-learning researcher at MIT.

The results do not mean that Astra, developed by OpenAI in San Francisco, California, can explain or understand how a given AI network works. But the findings suggest that general-purpose AI models — such as ChatGPT or Claude — might be able to modify a network in useful ways, like a mechanic who can identify and fix issues in an engine that they neither designed nor fully understand.

Researchers already try to interpret how different components of a network create its outputs. The preprint shows that it is possible to automate some of these ‘interpretability’ methods, says Fazl Barez, an AI-safety researcher at the University of Oxford, UK.

Researchers hope that better understanding models in this way will help to create safer AI systems, although Barez cautions that this assumption is “largely untested”.

It remains unclear if Astra is going beyond applying information and techniques learned in its training. Barez says he would be surprised if Astra is able to read and interpret models in ways that go beyond existing human abilities.

Three reasons why AI is not conscious and perhaps never will be

Three reasons why AI is not conscious and perhaps never will be

Still, if developed further, such ability to reprogram models might be an asset in developing AI for science, says Marinka Zitnik, a computer scientist and bioinformatician at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts. For example, it could help to spot errors in a model ahead of real-world testing, she says.

Frontier AI systems are based on massive neural networks — brain-inspired architectures in which layers of processing units, or neurons, are linked by billions of ‘weights’, values that represent the strength of connections inside a model. The strength of each weight is slowly nudged during training to make the model better at, for example, predicting a protein structure or the next word in a sentence.

The complex way in which a model’s features link to its outputs means they are often described as black boxes. Interpretability researchers run experiments to work out, for example, which weights are activated under specific conditions. Researchers have also previously developed custom models that can learn to edit other models2.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03679-8

The now 30-year-old may be without a club but was not so foolish as to not prepare for life without a bumper contract, with his company boasting the sizeable sum in assets.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an important block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

Former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

Palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik

Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David

Welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”

How long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

Looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap

The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the new season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

They have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

Another new arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

Alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

Juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. Lois Openda and Randal Kolo Muani have been signed this summer to strengthen the forward line.

#1727. Ramos speaks out after disappointing Portugal result vs. Denmark: “Something that happens”

AC Milan are, once again, left looking at a disappointing performance from Goncalo Ramos; this time it was for Portugal.

It’s fair to say that Ramos’ start to life with Milan has been unsatisfactory. The Portuguese started brightly in his first two games, but has since struggled to really hit the highs expected of him after an almost €90 million deal was agreed in the summer.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With another international break, the hope was that he’d rediscover the form from the last set of games and bring it back to San Siro, but it hasn’t happened that way yet.

Speaking in the mixed zone after Portugal’s heavy defeat, Ramos looked at what went wrong in the game and what needs to be corrected next time, as MilanPress relays.

“I think it was a tough match. They studied our team well, and even the details ultimately fell in their favour. Then we ended up losing momentum a bit, but that’s something that happens and is part of it.

“We’re first in the most important group. We already have another match in three days, so it’s not worth dwelling too much on what happened today. There’s already a match ahead, and it’s very important.”

“In the end, they managed to apply better pressure on us. We weren’t able to find many options, and that ended up hurting our game because we like to have clean, controlled possession of the ball, and that’s what makes the difference in our game.

“On the one hand, it’s good to have a match in three days and not have to spend three or four months thinking about a defeat like that. We already have a game to respond and to erase what happened here today.

“The conversation in the locker room after the game was that we’re first and we have a game to clean up after what happened today. That’s the goal of the team and the group.”

Considering he’s now the out-and-out first-choice striker for Portugal, it’s a lot of pressure on his shoulders for club and country. Hopefully he can start to thrive under the pressure, rather than succumbing to it.

#1726. Flamengo vs Athletico Paranaense - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 17 Nov 2026 19:11

With four rounds remaining in the Brasileirao, Flamengo host Athletico Paranaense on Wednesday night, November 18, as their title defence enters its decisive stage.

Having collected 92% of the available points in the second half of the season, Flamengo can take a significant step towards back-to-back titles and put themselves in a stronger position ahead of their huge clash against Palmeiras in the following round. Athletico Paranaense, meanwhile, face an uphill task to break back into the top four, having gone four matches without a win and with the tournament's leading scorer unavailable.

In the fight for back-to-back titles and a ninth Brasileirao crown, Flamengo return from this FIFA international break with good news: their key players delivered excellent performances and, more importantly, came back from international duty without any injuries.

Giorgian de Arrascaeta once again took centre stage for the Rubro-Negro with the Uruguay national team. Having had a direct hand in both of Uruguay’s goals against Argentina at the Bombonera, Flamengo’s number 10 also became the first foreigner to have a bust unveiled at the club’s headquarters, in a ceremony on Sunday, November 15.

Bruno Henrique also received the honour and looked ahead to the business end of the season: “We know there is not much left before the year ends, there are four games, so we will give everything in these games to win the title. God willing, we can celebrate in December as well,” he said at the event.

Right-back Guillermo Varela, meanwhile, produced a solid display, playing the full 95 minutes of the match in Buenos Aires. Although Argentina’s goal came down his side, he was not at fault.

Nicolas de la Cruz and Ecuadorians Gonzalo Plata and Anthony Valencia did not leave the bench, but the latter two still have a friendly against Bolivia on Tuesday night, November 17.

Athletico Paranaense, for their part, are enjoying a notable campaign for a newly promoted side. However, in the fight for a direct spot in next season’s Libertadores, the Furacao suffered a heavy blow at Brazil’s sports court (STJD).

In a hearing on Monday, November 16, Kevin Viveros had his ban extended to three matches. The Brasileirão’s top scorer with 21 goals was sent off in the 3-1 defeat to Vasco on November 4, for a stamp on full-back Cuiabano.

As a result, he will not return until the final round, against Sao Paulo at the Arena da Baixada. Jorge Rivaldo and Renan Peixoto are the natural options given their profile, but manager Odair Hellmann could also opt to use forward Kerwin Vargas in an adapted role.

In the same hearing, the Parana side were also punished. The fine for racist gestures attributed to a fan during the match against Vasco was increased to R$30,000 (approximately £4,200). The decision was taken by a majority of votes.

Currently fifth with 54 points, Athletico could close the gap on Fluminense, who occupy the final Libertadores spot. Bahia and Atletico Mineiro, however, are also in the same points range.

In a late development, Gonzalo Plata was released from the Ecuador squad for “personal reasons” and could become an unexpected boost. Having played just 13 minutes against Costa Rica, he should not, in theory, show any physical wear.

Nicolas de la Cruz and Anthony Valencia remain with their national teams and are not expected to return in time.

On the medical front, experienced left-back Alex Sandro has recovered from muscular oedema in his left thigh and has returned to training with the group, although Ayrton Lucas is expected to be the first choice for Portuguese manager Leonardo Jardim.

Midfielder Lucas Paqueta has not yet fully recovered from a knee problem sustained during the thrashing of Vasco, so he is unlikely to be included without a reasonable amount of training, according to Jardim himself. Danilo, meanwhile, continues his recovery schedule following a jaw fracture and also remains sidelined.

The point of concern is the number of players one booking away from suspension: Leo Pereira, Alex Sandro, Erick Pulgar, Arrascaeta, Pedro, Bruno Henrique, Luiz Araujo and Vitao. Should any of them be booked by referee Rafael Klein, they would miss the clash against Palmeiras in the following round.

Besides Viveros, Dantas is also serving a suspension due to the automatic one-match ban for a third yellow card. Young centre-back Arthur Dias, who is attracting interest from several European clubs, is another absentee. He is set to play for the Brazil national team against Singapore and is not expected to return to Brazil in time.

Defender Lucas Esquivel is still recovering from a hip injury and will be assessed on matchday, but he is expected to complete the back line alongside Gaston Benavidez and Juan Aguirre. Goalkeeper Santos and Bruno Zapelli could be given a chance in the starting eleven.

Agustin Rossi; Varela, Leo Pereira, Leo Ortiz, Ayrton Lucas; Pulgar, Jorginho, Arrascaeta; Carrascal, Pedro, Samuel Lino. Manager: Leonardo Jardim.

Athletico Paranaense possible starting lineup:

Santos; Benavidez, Aguirre, Esquivel; Gilberto, Luiz Gustavo, Jadson, Mendoza; Bruno Zapelli, Joao Cruz, Kerwin Vargas. Manager: Odair Hellmann.

Athletico's task would have been difficult enough as it is, but with their top scorer and best defender both unavailable, it is hard to see the visitors taking anything from this encounter.

For Flamengo, the priority will be to maintain their formidable home record and head into the most eagerly anticipated game of the year in a favourable position. A convincing victory at the Maracana would be the ideal way to achieve that.

#1725. Chelsea news: Estevao Willian provides fresh comments on playing time frustration after latest Brazil appearance

By Darren Plant | 17 Nov 2026 20:14

Chelsea winger Estevao Willian has thanked Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti for his "trust" during the international break.

The 19-year-old's lack of starts for Chelsea since the arrival of Xabi Alonso has been a regular topic of conversation.

Although the Spaniard placed more faith in the playmaker prior to the November international break, Estevao was still dropped after an encouraging performance versus Manchester United on October 31.

However, Ancelotti has recently insisted that Estevao's game time for Chelsea will not negatively impact on his role for the national team.

That stance has since been proven through the former Palmeiras starlet featuring for 128 minutes across friendlies versus Japan and Singapore.

During Tuesday's 7-0 win over Singapore, Estevao contributed one goal and two assists before his 70th-minute withdrawal.

Speaking to ESPN after the game, Estevao admitted that he was grateful for the support that he had received from Ancelotti.

He said: "I'm very happy to have gotten minutes in the friendlies.

"I thank Ancelotti for his confidence, because every player wants to play and at Chelsea I've had few minutes, but coming here and knowing that the manager trusts me gives me a lot of motivation."

With Kallang - the venue for Tuesday's friendly - eight hours in front of England, Estevao is essentially getting extra rest ahead of Saturday's Premier League game versus Leeds United.

Nevertheless, not only will it take his body clock time to reset, the likes of Cole Palmer, Danny Welbeck and Emanuel Emegha - players competing for roles in the final third - have not represented their countries during the international break.

Meanwhile, Morgan Rogers was back in the country on Monday after representing England, so Estevao is essentially at a disadvantage when it comes to trying to dislodge teammates from the starting lineup.

All things considered, it is highly likely that he will take a place on the substitutes' bench.

#1724. ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

“We did the first one quite well in a lot of moments but the compete part – especially in and around our box – was not to the standards to win a football match against a good side. It’s better to give them [the goals away] in a friendly match than an official match. It’s always good when you lose a match in pre-season because it creates a bit more fire in the belly.”

Kepa Arrizabalaga will not want to watch Betis’s first goal back in a hurry. The Arsenal goalkeeper may have got a slight nudge as he came for the ball at a corner but he was all over the place and never looked even in the vaguest control of the situation. Rodrigo Riquelme scored at the far post after the ball sailed over the keeper. Arteta called it a “really sloppy goal”. With former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier having arrived on a free transfer as back-up to Raya, Kepa faces an uncertain future at Arsenal. Moments like this will not help his cause.

He did not feature much last season but is probably best remembered for his torrid showing in the Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City in March. He looked as unconvincing here as he did then, as the former Chelsea goalkeeper also sliced a clearance in the build up to Betis’s third goal. Before then, Kai Havertz had turned over possession cheaply from which Nelson Deossa set up former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals to score.

Arsenal need more creativity and firepower in attack, hence the interest in Vinícius and Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez. Viktor Gyokeres again looked rather limited here and the likes of Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze are also still to report back. Yet one of the few, brighter aspects of Arsenal’s performances was the sight of the regal looking Riccardo Calafiori marauding forward from a very nominal left-back role.

If Arsenal are going to play more adventurously this season and try to ratchet up things in the entertainment stakes then Calafiori could have a big role to play, as long as Arteta can keep him fit. He can be a potent weapon galloping forward and there were clear glimpses of that here. Harnessing that talent while not compromising too much defensive security may be one of the manager’s challenges.

Louie Copley had only been on the pitch for nine minutes – a half-time substitute for Ben White – when the 19-year-old midfielder went down largely unchallenged with what looked like a troubling knee injury. Arteta admitted afterwards that the way the teenager fell to the ground was a concern and he looked in visible pain and distress as he was treated by the medical staff before being helped off the pitch.

The fear will be of some kind of ligament damage and Arteta confirmed Copley would be scanned on Thursday. “Quite worried to be fair for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive and the symptoms that he already has,” the manager said. “So we are going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. Touch wood that is not a bad one.”

🌴 @RealBetis_en's Hector Bellerin reacts to a 3-1 preseason win over his former club Arsenal"I spent 10 years over there always trying to help and see Arsenal where it belongs, and it's nice to finally face them with them being in that position" 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/er3YtAysQb

Since Gyokeres misses that very good chance just a minute into the game, Arsenal have not really carved out many genuine opportunities in front of goal, other than that Tzolis wasted chance. Every time they reach the final third, they are lacking that cutting edge.

Calafiori’s role is interesting. He’s very nominally a left back but is routinely stepping into midfield and raiding forward, often ending up in positions you’d associate with a No. 10. It’s the kind of role Nico O’Reilly played under Pep Guardiola at Manchester City.

Valles is so, so lucky. The Betis keeper inexplicably passes the ball straight at Tzolis inside the Betis penalty area but Tzolis is unable to capitalise. That is a huge slice of luck for Valles as that was a ridiculous moment.

Betis have already scored one goal from a corner and they now have another corner after Nwaneri’s clearance behind. The inswinger is sent into a good area but this time Arsenal deal with the danger.

Arsenal were the better side in the early stages but Betis have grown into this and have taken confidence from that goal.

Calafiori may be on the teamsheet tonight for Arsenal at left-back but when they are in possession the Italian is moving into midfield. Lewis-Skelly, who is playing in the number six role, is dropping in between the two centre-backs when Arsenal have the ball.

Betis win a free-kick out on the left, with the chance to send it into the Arsenal penalty area for the first time tonight. It is clipped into a good area but Kepa is out of his goal to catch it.

Arsenal should be ahead one minute into the game with their first attack of the game. Havertz picks up the ball on the corner of the box out on the left and passes it inside to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes one touch before shooting from the edge of the six-yard box but his shot is saved. In reality, Gyokeres should not have given Valles in the Betis goal any chance of saving that one.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, Arsenal led out by Ben White and Betis by former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin, and make their way past the Premier League trophy. We are moments away from kick-off in Dublin.

#1722. Egypt sack their manager for 'negative impact on team image' after he fainted when fight broke out between his TWO wives with punches and hair-pulling in a bar

Published: 13:16 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 13:48 EST, 13 November 2026

Egypt will begin their African Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying matches with a new manager after their previous head coach was sacked amid a torrid breakdown of both of his marriages.

Hossam Hassan was handed his marching orders on Saturday after an incident in August which saw his two wives embroiled in a vicious fight, captured and shared on social media.

Hassan's first wife Howaida El-Gharbawy and his second Dina 'Dan Adam' Mustafa started the argument while at a hotel bar in the upscale Porto Marina resort on Egypt's north coast.

El-Gharbawy and Mustafa were videoed arguing with Hassan in the middle attempting to cool tensions, but the duo came to blows, with punches thrown and hair pulled as screams filled the air.

Such was the stress of the incident that Hassan is believed to have fainted as he tried to separate the two women.

Horrified public onlookers watched as the physical fight grew with relatives of the trio getting involved, and security was called before Hassan was taken to hospital.

En Égypte, un violent différend a éclaté entre... les deux femmes du sélectionneur égyptien, Hossam Hassan. 🇪🇬😳Le conflit a dégénéré en échauffourée avec coups et tirage de cheveux, avant que des jeunes et des passages n'interviennent dans la bagarre. pic.twitter.com/pvRUSMtAsD

Egypt head coach Hossam Hassan was sacked this week after a fight broke out between his two wives

Hassan's first wife Howaida El-Gharbawy and his second Dina 'Dan Adam' Mustafa started the argument while at a hotel in the upscale Porto Marina resort

The 60-year-old is believed to have fainted while trying to separate the two women

Both women are believed to have been left with cuts and bruises following the vicious scrap, while Hassan, despite briefly losing consciousness, was left unharmed.

His lawyers later told Sky News Arabia, via the Sun, that he was not suffering a health crisis during the incident, and that he remained in good health.

But in the days that followed, Hassan started proceedings to divorce El-Gharbawy, who he has been married to for decades. The couple also share three children.

The 60-year-old has a further two children with second wife Mustafa, who Le Parisien alleges also filed for divorce in the days after the footage went viral on social media.

The Egyptian Football Association ensured that Hassan's professional life took a similar nosedive, sharing in a statement that his dismissal was due in part to reputational damage the scandal might be doing to the national team.

'After analysing all the circumstances and events of the past few days, as well as their consequences and the negative impact they have had on the positive image and stability of our national team, the Board of Directors has decided, within the framework of its responsibilities, to dismiss coach Hossam Hassan and his entire technical staff and to end his tenure,' their statement read.

Mustafa's lawyer Mohamed Shams gave an interview on Sky News Arabia claiming that his client had been the victim of a 'premeditated attack'.

'We hoped it wouldn't come to divorce, but things escalated to this level.'

Hassan married his second wife in 2015, with Egyptian law allowing Muslim men to marry up to four women, providing that any wives have been formally informed that another marriage is to take place.

The law mandates that the husband is also obligated to treat all of his wives equally with regard to housing, financial support and standard of living.

Hassan had been married to his first wife El-Gharbawy for decades, with the pair sharing three of his five children

Hassan and Mustafa briefly separated four years ago before recoupling before the spat that ended both of his marriages.

As well as being relieved of his duties, Hassan was also sanctioned by the Supreme Council for Media Regulation, leaving him unable to publicly address the media following his sacking.

Mohamed Salah and Co will now play their first qualifier of the international break against Malawi under new head coach Ali Maher.

The former Liverpool star could be among those Pharaohs stars privately pleased with the departure of Hassan, after he was benched by his ex-manager for the last two international clashes.

When asked why the superstar and national team captain had been left on the sidelines for the ties, Hassan had said: 'It is not right for a country of 120 million people for the national team to depend on one player.'

#1721. Tottenham urged to sign £12.5m midfielder who would be "top five" in Premier League

By Ben Knapton | 17 Nov 2026 20:21, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 20:21

Tottenham Hotspur have been urged to make an approach for AC Milan midfielder Youssouf Fofana, who could be one of the "top five" players in his position in the Premier League.

The Lilywhites spent big to reinforce their engine room during the summer with the signings of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes for a combined £185m, while Rodrigo Bentancur, Lucas Bergvall and Conor Gallagher remain on the books too.

However, a report from Italian outlet Calciomercato states that Tottenham are 'ready to attack' for Fofana, who is currently on loan at Sevilla from Milan and has made a positive impression in La Liga.

Fofana has scored one goal and provided three assists in nine Spanish top-flight appearances, but he is only under contract with Milan until 2028, and his long-term future remains unclear.

Speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, former Milan striker Mark Hateley implored Tottenham to make a move for Fofana, whom he believes everyone would be casting their eye on if he became available.

"That's the type of player all top clubs would look for, even as a bit-part player," Hateley said. "He's one of those players who'll get into the side and be good in it, and then out of the side if need be.

“There are a lot better players out there, but he is a good player. That's the difference between the top three, four, five clubs now. You can pay £50m or £60m for a guy who's just going to be knocking around the squad, and that's where we are in the football world right now.

“He'd be one of the top three, four or five in England anyway; we'd all be looking at that sort of player if he became available.

“Spurs are still struggling to find something at the moment. It's normally the player you never imagine is going to make everybody else work: the squad player, your £30m or £40m, maybe £50m player, and it works.

“That's where we are with Tottenham right now. I've seen them play very well this season, but I've also seen them play very, very poorly, and that's the frustration with supporters, because you don't know which team is going to turn up. It's not an 11 you're building right now, it's an 18 or 19-man starting line-up."

Reportedly valued at just £12.5m by AC Milan, Fofana does not trump his Spurs rivals in many statistical columns, but the 27-year-old is superior to Fernandes, Tonali, Gallagher and Bentancur on a few metrics.

Fofana's 0.38 assists per 90 minutes is the highest total among the quintet, as is his 1.15 successful dribbles per game, from 3.56 attempts; Gallagher is second in the latter statistic with 1.42.

Fofana has also been dispossessed on the fewest occasions - just 0.76 times per 90 minutes - and was no stranger to a direct involvement during his first two seasons with Milan.

The ex-Monaco man has scored three goals and set up 13 more in 88 games for the Rossoneri, although he was left out of France's World Cup squad and has not represented Les Bleus since 2024.

Mark Hateley was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of London.Bet.

#1719. Wayne Rooney opens up on mental health struggles, drinking and seeking help from a therapist

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 20:39

Wayne Rooney has revealed that he contemplated suicide during his time at Manchester United. The former England captain, 41, spoke about it on the Life at the Midpoint podcast, hosted by Gabby Logan, describing a period when his eldest son Kai was still a baby. The interview was reported by the BBC and also picked up by Sky Sports.

‘I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide,’ Rooney said. ‘You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops.’

Rooney was speaking about years when he was at his best on the pitch. According to the BBC, Kai is now 17, so the period was roughly 17 years ago. He describes it as a time when he had just got married and just had a son.

‘It should be the happiest point in my life, and it wasn’t,’ he said. Asked by Logan about the hardest moment of his life, he said that when he was drinking he would shut himself at home for two days and just drink, at what was probably the best phase of his career in playing terms.

He joined United from Everton in 2004 and, according to the BBC, became the club’s all-time top scorer with 253 goals in 559 games. He won five Premier League titles, the Champions League, the Europa League, the FA Cup and three League Cups before returning to Everton in 2017. He remains a legend at Old Trafford, where Mauricio Pochettino is now beginning his time as boss.

‘I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else, I really struggled with it,’ he said on the podcast.

Rooney also explained why nothing showed on the outside at the time. ‘You don’t want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it,’ he said. He said a feeling that he would be less of a man stopped him admitting his own state. In the end he confided in his wife Coleen and his mother and started speaking to a therapist. He now describes his behaviour at the time as selfish. ‘Coleen helped me enormously,’ he added. ‘She could have left, it was that bad, but she stayed by me and helped me get through it.’

This is not the first time Rooney has spoken about a dark period. In February 2022, when the Rooney documentary came out on Amazon Prime Video and he was managing Derby County, he told the PA news agency, as reported by The42, that he suffered inside for a long part of his career and that a lot of it ended in drinking. He also told the Mail on Sunday, as reported by Inside World Football, that in his early years at United, until about the birth of Kai, he would shut himself at home and drink. He pointed to the pressure of playing for England and United and what the newspapers wrote about his private life. According to PA, he saw a psychologist only briefly at the time.

The new interview is a significant step on from those earlier accounts. In the 2022 pieces, the subjects were alcohol and the pressure of fame, with no mention of suicidal thoughts. Rooney did, however, explain then why he stayed silent as a player. He said he could not go to older players such as Roy Keane or Ryan Giggs and say there was a problem. He added that today it is much easier, because mental health is talked about and problems are caught earlier, especially among young players.

England’s most famous striker of his generation could not speak about his state while he was playing, and speaks most openly about it as a former player and television pundit. He has been named pundit of the year at the Broadcast Sport Awards and currently appears in the ITV reality show I’m a Celebrity. The subject has remained relevant in dressing rooms, as goalkeeper James Trafford showed recently when he left Manchester City over his mental health.

If you or someone you know is struggling, support is available. In the UK, Samaritans can be called free at any time on 116 123.
